newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria appoints high-powered economic plan team.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria appoints high-powered economic plan team.

text.p: Nigeria's military leader General Sani Abacha on Tuesday set up a committee to develop an economic plan into the next century.

"To ensure the success of the Vision 2010 government has decided to set up a high powered committee headed by Chief Ernest Shonekan, a former head of state and industrialist of international repute," Abacha said in a speech on the 36th anniversary of Nigeria's independence.
Shonekan, a former chairman of Nigerian conglomerate UAC is seen as an apostle of International Monetary Fund style economic deregulation.
"The committee .. will be composed of representatives from all sectors of the economy and public life," Abacha said.
"It will specifically examine those aspects of the economy which should be developed and strengthened."
The crude-oil dependent economy of Africa's most populous nation has been in the doldrums since political crisis erupted in 1993, with the annulment of elections by a previous military government.
Abacha's tight fiscal policy in 1994 and 1995 is credited with reducing inflation and stabilising the naira currency, but there are scant signs of economic growth.
The military government, under fire from western countries for alleged human rights abuses and lack of democracy, has said it will hand over power to civilians by October 1998.
